thread:
maya: fyi -> vendor posted advisory for cryptography (CVE-2026-2390). patch available (40.1.1). EPSS ~0.67, CVSS 9.1. appears in kms-client and our serving runtime deps. tagging for quick triage. :eyes:
samir: link to advisory? any known PoC?
maya: https://example.com/advisories/CVE-2026-2390 (vendor). advisory says memory corruption in X509 parsing, remote exploit with crafted cert. no full PoC published yet, but exploitability flagged.
olivia: quick repo grep: `grep -R "cryptography" -n deps/ third_party/` shows kms-client/requirements.txt -> cryptography==40.0.2 and runtime/docker/requirements.txt -> cryptography>=40.0.0,<41.0.0. so both pinned to 40.x
henry: thanks. if runtime pulls >=40 but <41 we need to ensure we bump to 40.1.1 or patch backport where needed.
sec-bot: vuln-scan: project:serving-runtime - cryptography 40.0.2 -> matched advisory CVE-2026-2390, severity HIGH, exploitability: PROOF_POSSIBLE, suggested fix: 40.1.1. (scan ts: 1947654342)
oncall: recommend immediate owner + canary patch in dedicated infra. window for emergency patching starts in 30m, ops oncall available. :alarm_clock:
samir: triage checklist: 1) exploit in wild? vendor: not published but EPSS 0.67. 2) reachable components? kms-client used in control-plane services (sensitive). serving-runtime uses cryptography for TLS certs in some internal agent flows; potentially exploitable. 3) patch avail? yes -> 40.1.1. 4) can we hotpatch without restart? probably requires rolling restart of affected services.
maya: agree. I'd mark KMS/control-plane as P0 (hotpatch now). app-facing runtime nodes P1 but schedule asap. can we produce a minimal canary job to validate 40.1.1?
olivia: quick test matrix: build container with cryptography==40.1.1, run integration cert-parsing tests, smoke agent TLS handshake tests. should take ~45m to get canary image. I can run it.
henry: we'll need to coordinate RBAC changes? not for this patch. but note: if any config reloads expose cert parsing endpoints, consider temporary rate-limiting.
oncall: ops: I'll hold a 1hr emergency slot, ready for rolling restarts in staging then prod canary.
maya: owner: @olivia on canary and PRs to bump pins. @samir ownpack to coordinate release checklist and backports for Dedicated. @henry run impact assessment for KMS-control-plane. I'll create issue and tag security-severity:critical.
samir: PR stub: `bump(cryptography): 40.0.2 -> 40.1.1` and backport PR for release-2025.1. will include changelog and test results.
olivia: running canary build now -> `docker build -f Dockerfile.runtime -t runtime:patch-crypto-40.1.1 .` then run `pytest tests/integration/test_cert_parsing.py -q`.
maya: good. also check third_party libs that vendor their own cryptography wheels (embeds) — I've seen one in analytics-agent. olivia pls grep for vendored wheels.
olivia: doing vendor check: `grep -R "cryptography" -n third_party | grep wheel || true` -> found analytics-agent/vendor/cryptography-40.0.2.whl. will open follow-up to replace wheel or rebuild with wheel from 40.1.1.
henry: note for Dedicated customers: some infra images are pinned to older Python 3.9 wheels. Samir please include backport plan and notify account execs if we need forced upgrades.
samir: will draft customer communication template after we confirm canary result.
oncall: status update: canary passed basic tests (ts:1947654360). ready for rolling patch to staging.
maya: thanks. plan: 1) open security-issue, assign owners (done), 2) canary -> staging -> prod (KMS/control-plane first), 3) backports for Dedicated/backed images, 4) customer comms if forced upgrade. target timeline: full prod rollout in 6 hours if no regressions.
henry: I'll also add temporary audit-logging increase around cert validation errors to detect exploitation attempts during rollout.
maya: ack. closing here once PRs and issue exist. keep updates in thread. :thumbsup:
